html:
A charter of rights that King John of England sealed at Runnymede, near Windsor, on 15 June 1215, to make peace with rebel barons. Its name is Latin for "Great Charter".

John, brother of Richard the Lionheart, had lost Normandy to Philip II of France and squeezed his barons with heavy taxes to win it back. After his allies were beaten at Bouvines in 1214, the barons rebelled and took London. The charter promised:

  • no extra taxes without the "common counsel" of the kingdom;
  • no free man to be jailed or stripped of his rights except by the lawful judgement of his peers or by the law of the land;
  • justice not to be sold, denied or delayed;
  • the rights of the church and of the City of London.

Neither side kept it. The pope annulled it within weeks, and war followed. But after John died in 1216 his son's guardians reissued it, and the version of 1225 became part of English law. Later, lawyers used it against the Stuart kings, and American colonists read its ideas into the US Constitution.
sum: A charter of rights that King John of England sealed at Runnymede, near Windsor, on 15 June 1215, to make peace with rebel barons. Its name is Latin for "Great Charter".
